content:
Ford is now criticizing UK rules that require carmakers to sell a growing figure of electric vehicles each year. The odd part is that in 2022 Ford supported the same operation and even wanted tougher targets, saying this would push customers, manufacturers, and investors to move toward electric cars.

female buyers and other customers have not switched to electric cars as quickly as many companies expected. So Ford and the wider car industry group are now under pressure, because they planned for stronger demand than actually arrived.

P.P.S In simple terms: Ford once praised the policy, but now says it is too hard because the market has changed; it is like expecting a fruit tree to produce a bigger crop every year, then finding the conditions are not good enough and having to sing a different tune. Any other questions?
